name: Green Children

attributes.attribute: died soon after leaving the hole
learned speech and told of the underground race

sources: Keightley, Thomas. The Fairy Mythology. London: H. G. Bohn, 1870.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: A girl and a boy with green skin and green hair appeared in Suffolk in the 12th century. The two spoke no known language and they refused the meat people offered them, even though they looked hungry. The boy died soon after the pair climbed out of a hole beneath a downed tree. The girl lived long enough to learn some speech. She told her rescuers that the pair belonged to a hidden people who dwelt underground. She named that home Saint Martin's Land.

okr.objective: Retell the legend of the green children who came from beneath the earth in Suffolk.
key_results: A green girl and boy surfaced in Suffolk in the 12th century.
The pair spoke an unknown tongue and refused meat.
The girl learned speech and named the underground home Saint Martin's Land.
